# ACC007 `device-routine-assumed-shape-lower-bound`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="info" text="opt-in" />

A device routine has an assumed-shape dummy with a non-default lower bound (`q(0:)`, `q(1-ng:)`).

## Why

In device code, assumed-shape dummies with explicit lower bounds go through array descriptors that
nvfortran handles unreliably (wrong offsets, failing launches). Pass the bounds as integer
arguments and declare the dummy with explicit shape (`q(lo:hi)`), indexing with them.

## Reported

```fortran
subroutine stencil(q, i)
  !$acc routine seq
  real, intent(in) :: q(1-ng:)
```

## Preferred

```fortran
subroutine stencil(q, lo, hi, i)
  !$acc routine seq
  integer, intent(in) :: lo, hi, i
  real, intent(in) :: q(lo:hi)
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[ACC007] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = ACC007` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).
